I planned iteration 0194 as step 4 of the positive-control thread (#763 f4). The graph has two tasks: an author task and a changed-scope review that waits for it (`blocked_by`).

Why: #831 ended partial with NOT-CLEAR, but for procedural reasons only. It answered F2 from the code: `compute()` checks the literal by exact equality, and the locator is checked only for grounding, through `citation_support()`. It also found that the self-test mutations cover only claim A0005, so A0001 and A0002 have no mutation controls. I closed F3 myself with one Grep: `benchmark/challenges/library-specialty.json:2513` sets `inventory_path` to `benchmark/cases/dev/library-specialty.json`. So the dev file is the inventory the scorer reads, not a copy. That leaves no open review question that blocks step 4.

- `positive-control-author-0194` (benchmark, default model, medium effort, 60 min / 45 turns): add wrong-literal and wrong-citation mutations for A0001 and A0002, answer F4 from the inventory's citation entries, regenerate `benchmark/results/challenges.json` and update every pin of a changed file.
- `positive-control-review-0194` (reviewer, default model, medium effort, 40 min / 30 turns): save the commit and file hashes first, run the self-test on a temporary copy outside the repository, then give a CLEAR or NOT-CLEAR verdict.

`.session/tasks.json` passed the direct Python JSON, field and heading check (exit 0). I updated `journal/working-memory.md` with the four sections.

## Discoveries
- Tools were disabled partway through two sessions in a row (#828, #831). If it happens again in 0194, it should go to the Policymaker as a suggestion (record `.session/history/records/0193.json`).
- The scorer never checks citations against the XML artifact, only against the inventory (#831 report). This is carried as a design limit in working memory.

## What next
Read the review verdict. On CLEAR, close the positive-control thread and pick the next method gap (independent confirmation of the XML key). On NOT-CLEAR, fix only the named findings. Do not re-derive the literals or reopen F3.
